title: Let me know if I should make a full review video for any of these :) ...
transcript: There are so many great plays happening off Broadway right now. Here are five that I think are worth your time. Okay, bear with me on this one. I love you so much I could die is by Mona Perneau, who wrote and starred in this deeply personal show. But the catch is that Mona actually does not talk in the show at all. In fact, she sits in a chair with her back towards the audience, and all of the dialogue in the show is read by a text to speech reader. The only time we actually hear Mona's voice are in a couple of songs that she wrote that are sprinkled throughout the piece that she plays on guitar, still with her back to the audience. I think this easily could have come across as very gimmicky, but once you see the show, I think it will become clear why this narrative choice was taken. And I found it to be really effective, and by the end, I was actually really emotional. I was surprised by how moved I was just listening to this robot's voice. Jonah is one of those plays that I saw months ago, and I have not stopped thinking about it since I saw it. The show is, at its core, and exploration on trauma and the way that we deal with it and grow and move on from it. As such, there are some intense scenes in the show, included one that is Very visceral, so definitely Trigger Warning. But if you are okay with a darker subject matter, I highly recommend the show. Gabby Beans is the lead character in this and she is giving one of the best performances I have ever seen. Like, I am not exaggerating when I say I will be thinking about her performance for years to come. I'm over here now! Job is a play that I saw last year, I think in October that totally blew my mind. It is one of those shows where it's not entirely clear what the show is about up front, and the show will give you a little bit more pieces of information as the show goes on. And it keeps you guessing and keeps you on the edge of your seat. And it is incredibly effective at that. It is one of those shows where at the end of it, I wanted to immediately go back and rewatch it so I could see all of the little hints that I may have missed along the way. It is currently doing an encore run at the Connolly Theater, and while I have not been able to see it at the new venue, I've heard it has only gotten better. My only piece of advice, having been to that theater before for another show, would be that the rear of that mezzanine is very obstructed, so I would definitely recommend sitting in the orchestra if you can. Seven Year Disappear Star Cynthia Nixon and Taylor Trench, both of whom are giving unreal performances. Cynthia Nixon especially gets to play multiple characters throughout the course of the show, and she absolutely bodies every single one of them. She's so good at the show. So itself is about performance art in the lengths that we go to make our art, as well as the relationship between a mother and son. It is, for the most part, told in reverse chronological order, similar to merrily we roll along. If you don't like non linear storytelling, the show may not be for you, but for me, it was like a little puzzle box, and I loved connecting all the bits and pieces as the scenes went backwards in time. I'm gonna keep this one short and sweet because I am hardly the first person on this app to tell you how amazing O Mary is, but boy, oh boy, doesn't live up to the hype. Is without hyperbole, one of the funniest plays I have ever seen, and Cole Escola is incredible in it. It is a farcical, funny, very silly, revisionist look at history and the relationship between Mary Todd Lincoln and Abraham Lincoln. Tickets for the initial run sold out super fast, but they just extended, so there may be tickets still left for the extension. Go grab them!
classificationReason: Creator explicitly frames as 'Here are five [off-Broadway plays] that I think are worth your time' and the title invites full review requests — a classic roundup of 5+ shows with no single focus.
